unit: none: the board has three families, each with its own unit, reference and floor (families[*].unit, .reference, .floor); S, ratio to reference and ratio to floor are comparable within a family and nowhere else
what_this_is: A view of frozen whole-pipeline ECDLP measurements, curve by curve, each against its own family's matched reference and generic floor. No new measurement.
what_this_is_not: a claim about any curve not on it

A.title: Koblitz, one target
A.status: primary comparison: one target, as AGENTS.md's one-target rule requires
A.targets: one unseen public point per process, 64 per size
A.unit: one batched affine addition (`add_many` over 1,024 subgroup points), per √r
A.unit_how: A clock reading, not a count: `ic price` times each phase exclusively, on one thread, and divides by this unit, measured around each repetition (§20, §23).
A.reference: One-target rho on the same point, measured as built (its set-up plus its walk), in the same unit and the same process; its answer replayed and verified (§23).
A.floor: √(π/4n) rho steps per √r: generic, one target, no precomputation, A = 2n by signed Frobenius and negation, n the extension degree. Stated in steps and not rescaled to units, so × floor here divides units by steps.

B.title: Prime and random-binary ladder
B.status: primary comparison: one target per instance
B.unit_how: A count, not a clock: exact native operation counts converted to additions at the dimensionless ratios pinned per instance in `docs/ic/calibration.json` (ns per native operation over ns per group addition; all 13 instances used the pinned ratios; `ic boundary`, ledger §12). No conversion to table A's or C's unit is applied or claimed.
B.reference: Matched Pollard rho on the same instance, one target: the negation-map r-adding walk (A = 2), counted in GAE, verified [d]G = Q (§18).
B.floor: √(π/4) ≈ 0.886 GAE per √r: generic, one target, no precomputation, A = 2 usable automorphisms (negation).

C.title: Koblitz, 32-target batch
C.status: historical diagnostic under AGENTS.md's one-target rule: 32 targets solved together
C.targets: 32 targets solved together, priced per target
C.unit: one batched affine addition (`add_many` over 1,024 subgroup points), per √r, per target
C.unit_how: A clock reading, not a count: `ic price` times each phase exclusively, on one thread, and divides by this unit (§20, §22 isolated re-run).
C.reference: Batch rho on the same 32 targets (signed Frobenius and negation), its counted operations priced at the canonical step, one batched addition plus the table canonicalisation, in the same process (§20). Collisions shared across the 32 targets are in its cost per target.
C.floor: L(32)·√(π/4n) steps per √r per target, with L(32) = 0.19869: the one-target floor of table A times Kuhn–Struik's batch share. Stated in steps and not rescaled to units, and a smaller object than table A's floor, so × floor in C and in A do not compare.

phases.name: Reusable set-up
phases.what: Base, pair table, relations and logs, built once and reusable across targets (one-target Koblitz rows, §23)

phases.name: Curve and subgroup
phases.what: Point count, factoring #E, generator, cofactor clearing

phases.name: Workflow constructions
phases.what: Orbit maps, point index, collectors and solvers built around the work (Koblitz rows)

phases.name: Factor base
phases.what: Choose and materialise the base points, or their orbit representatives

phases.name: Pair table
phases.what: Every pair sum of the base, stored for meet-in-the-middle lookups

phases.name: Relations (PDP)
phases.what: Draw targets and decompose each over the base: the point decomposition problem

phases.name: Linear algebra
phases.what: Eliminate over Z/rZ until the target's column, or every base log, is pinned

phases.name: Descent
phases.what: Decompose each target over the logged base (Koblitz rows; the ladder puts the target in the matrix)

phases.name: Verification
phases.what: Re-add every relation and check [d]G = Q
